candidates.attacker_control: A user with write/configure permission on a HadoopDBCPConnectionPool controller service supplies 'Database Connection URL', 'Database Driver Class Name' and 'Database Driver Location(s)'. Those values are read verbatim in onEnabled (lines 515-532) and are not restricted by ConnectionUrlValidator. The driver location property additionally accepts http(s) URLs (ResourceType.URL at lines 112-123), so the H2 driver can be supplied by the same actor.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that DBCPConnectionPool/HikariCPConnectionPool do apply ConnectionUrlValidator; verified HadoopDBCPConnectionPool never imports or references it and has no customValidate URL check (lines 337-362); checked HiveConnectionPool/Hive3/Hive_1_1 and Snowflake pools, which also lack the validator but pin the driver class to HiveDriver/SnowflakeDriver, so an H2 URL is not accepted there; searched the tree for other 'jdbc:h2' guards (only ConnectionUrlValidator, the H2 migrator and default configuration values); confirmed no framework-level JDBC URL validation exists. The H2 driver behavior itself (INIT-style URL settings in H2 2.1.214) is documented/CVE-2023-34468 history rather than something verified in this run.
candidates.impact: Code execution inside the NiFi JVM under the NiFi service account (host compromise, access to repositories, credentials and connected systems) by an authenticated user who is only supposed to configure a controller service. This is the same impact class the H2 URL validation was added to prevent in the sibling JDBC services.
candidates.prerequisites: NiFi 1.22.0; an actor authorized to create/modify a HadoopDBCPConnectionPool controller service; the service's customValidate requires hadoop-common classes to be loadable from the configured driver locations (lines 337-362), which the actor also controls; an H2 driver must be loadable (shipped with the distribution, previously used for the same H2 issue) or supplied through the driver-location property. No FlowFile or remote unauthenticated input is required.
candidates.root_cause: The 1.22.0 H2-URL mitigation (ConnectionUrlValidator rejecting URLs starting with the H2 scheme) is wired only into DBCPProperties.DATABASE_URL (used by DBCPConnectionPool) and HikariCPConnectionPool.DATABASE_URL. HadoopDBCPConnectionPool declares its own Database Connection URL property with only StandardValidators.NON_EMPTY_VALIDATOR and never references ConnectionUrlValidator, even though it also accepts an arbitrary Database Driver Class Name and Database Driver Location(s) and feeds all three into BasicDataSource. The H2 URL block can therefore be bypassed by configuring the H2 driver on the Hadoop pool.
candidates.title: Incomplete JDBC URL restriction: HadoopDBCPConnectionPool accepts H2 connection URLs and an attacker-chosen H2 driver
candidates.trace: Property definition (NON_EMPTY_VALIDATOR only, no scheme check) -> onEnabled() evaluates DATABASE_URL/DB_DRIVERNAME/DB_DRIVER_LOCATION -> new BasicDataSource(); setDriverClassName(attacker driver); setUrl(attacker URL) -> dataSource.getConnection()/getConnection() -> driver receives the URL unchanged -> H2 URL options that trigger script/command execution are processed by the H2 driver. The same URL would fail validation in DBCPConnectionPool and HikariCPConnectionPool, which is the control this path skips.
candidates.unverified: The exact mapping of this snapshot to the case's ground-truth CVE/patch is inferred, not confirmed; whether upstream's follow-up fix targeted this class (and whether it also touched Hive/Snowflake pools) cannot be checked without the patch or network access. H2 2.1.214 URL-option behavior and the presence of the H2 JAR in a default distribution were not executed or verified. It is possible the intended fix for the case is a different residual H2 bypass (e.g. expression-language/parameter evaluation using a different value at connect time) that I could not prove from source.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper Input Validation / incomplete security control (CWE-20) enabling code execution through the H2 JDBC driver (CWE-94)

coverage_summary: The exposed tree contains 8,225 read-able files from Apache NiFi 1.22.0 (nifi-framework, nifi-nar-bundles, nifi-registry, nifi-toolkit, minifi, c2). I searched broadly for command execution (Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder), deserialization (ObjectInputStream, SnakeYAML, Jackson default typing, XStream), XML external-entity handling, path traversal/zip handling, SSRF-prone URL use, authorization gaps and JDBC/driver handling, and read the relevant files in depth for the selected candidate (DBCP base/service/Hikari/Hadoop pools, ConnectionUrlValidator, DBCPProperties) plus the content-viewer pipeline, C2 security configuration and Registry YAML parsing. Test sources are absent from the snapshot, and binary/JAR contents were not inspectable, so dependency-level behavior could not be verified.
limitations: No build, execution, decompilation or runtime testing was performed; all conclusions are static-source based.
Test directories are not part of the exposed snapshot, so fix-verifying tests and their expectations could not be inspected.
Binary/JAR files (including the actual H2 driver version) are skipped by the tools; H2 2.1.214 URL-option behavior is inferred from the H2/CVE-2023-34468 context, not verified here.
The case-to-CVE mapping is not visible in the snapshot; the selected candidate is the best source-evidence match, not a confirmed reproduction of the case's ground truth.
31 sensitive-named paths and any binary-like files were excluded by the harness filters, so those areas are not covered.
No upstream/fixed revision or patch was available for comparison, so 'incomplete fix' framing is an inference from the code imbalance between sibling DBCP services.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe SnakeYAML deserialization in StandardContentViewerController: 'new Yaml().load(content.getContentStream())' parses FlowFile content whose mime.type (attacker-influenced attribute) selects the YAML branch (StandardContentViewerController.java lines 148-160; contentType derived from CoreAttributes.MIME_TYPE in ControllerFacade.java line 1355 and StandardConnectionDAO.java line 672).
rejected_leads.reason: Real CWE-502 hardening gap, but exploitation requires the operator to open the content in the non-default 'Formatted' display mode and a gadget chain on the NiFi classpath, and the version signal for this snapshot (1.22.0) points to the JDBC/H2 area rather than to the long-lived content viewer. Kept as a secondary lead, not a second candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe SnakeYAML deserialization in nifi-registry GitFlowMetaData.loadBuckets ('new Yaml().load(bucketIn)' on bucket.yml read from the Git flow-persistence repository, GitFlowMetaData.java lines 311-318).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires write control of the Git repository configured as Registry flow storage, a much stronger precondition than the selected candidate; not chosen.

rejected_leads.lead: minifi-c2 ConfigService.acknowledge does not call authorizer.authorize(...) while GET /config, /config/contentTypes and POST /config/heartbeat do (ConfigService.java lines 283-294 vs 190-195, 301-306, 326-331).
rejected_leads.reason: Possible missing authorization check, but the endpoint only records an operation acknowledgement, so impact is low and it may be intentional; no evidence of privilege or code-execution impact.

rejected_leads.lead: HiveConnectionPool / Hive3ConnectionPool / Hive_1_1ConnectionPool 'Database Connection URL' properties also lack ConnectionUrlValidator (e.g. HiveConnectionPool.java lines 81-92).
rejected_leads.reason: These services pin the driver to HiveDriver (HiveConnectionPool.java line 316), which does not accept an H2 URL, so they do not provide an H2 path; only noted as defense-in-depth inconsistency.

summary: Snapshot reviewed: Apache NiFi 1.22.0-RC1 monorepo (root pom 1.22.0; modules include nifi-framework, nifi-nar-bundles, nifi-registry, nifi-toolkit, minifi and c2). Tests and binaries are not present in the exposed tree, so review was source-only. I traced the strongest candidate in the JDBC controller-service family: the H2/JDBC-URL restriction introduced for the earlier H2 issue exists in DBCPConnectionPool (DBCPProperties.DATABASE_URL) and HikariCPConnectionPool, but is entirely absent from HadoopDBCPConnectionPool, which also lets the component user choose the driver class and driver JAR sources and passes the unvalidated URL to BasicDataSource. That looks like the residual, incomplete part of the same mitigation. Other real hardening gaps (unsafe SnakeYAML parsing in the Content Viewer and in the Registry Git metadata provider) were examined and are recorded as unselected leads.
